record.paper_title: Variation Structures: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Given an ε-hermitian variation structure V=(U;b,ρ,V) of a group G, Wall's triple-kernel signature defines a homogeneous 2-cocycle σ(V;·,·,·) and hence a semigroup morphism c1:HVε(G)->H^2(G,Z). What are the higher-dimensional analogues of this class c1 in H^{2q}(G,Z)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\varepsilon=\pm 1$ and let $G$ be a group. An $\varepsilon$-hermitian variation structure over $G$ is a quadruple $\mathcal V=(U;b,\rho,V)$ where $U$ is a finite-dimensional complex vector space, $b:U\times U\to\mathbb C$ is a non-degenerate $\varepsilon$-hermitian form, $\rho:G\to\mathrm{Aut}(U,b)$ is a representation of $G$ by $b$-isometries, and $V:U\to U$ is a linear endomorphism satisfying the compatibility axioms of a variation map (in particular $b(Vx,y)+\varepsilon\,\overline{b(y,Vx)}=$ the prescribed pairing, and $V$ intertwines with $\rho$). Isomorphism classes of such structures, under orthogonal direct sum, form an abelian semigroup $HV^{\varepsilon}(G)$.

For three $\rho$-invariant Lagrangian-type kernels $K_1,K_2,K_3\subset U$ associated with $\mathcal V$, Wall's triple-kernel signature produces an integer $\sigma(\mathcal V;K_1,K_2,K_3)\in\mathbb Z$. Considering $\mathbb Z$ as a trivial $G$-module, the assignment $(g_1,g_2,g_3)\mapsto \sigma(\mathcal V;g_1K_0,g_1g_2K_0,g_1g_2g_3K_0)$ (for a fixed reference kernel $K_0$) is a homogeneous $2$-cocycle on $G$, and one obtains a semigroup morphism
$$c_1:HV^{\varepsilon}(G)\longrightarrow H^2(G,\mathbb Z),\qquad c_1(\mathcal V)=[\sigma(\mathcal V;\cdot,\cdot,\cdot)],$$
which is non-trivial in general.

Problem. Construct, for every integer $q\geq 1$, natural higher-dimensional analogues
$$c_q:HV^{\varepsilon}(G)\longrightarrow H^{2q}(G,\mathbb Z)$$
of $c_1$, defined from the variation-structure data $(U;b,\rho,V)$, that generalize the Wall triple-kernel signature cocycle and recover $c_1$ when $q=1$. Investigate their non-triviality and their relations (products, Whitney-type formulas) as characteristic classes of $\varepsilon$-hermitian variation structures of $G$.

artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search for higher-dimensional analogues of the Wall-Chern class $c_1$ on hermitian variation structures in $H^{2q}(G,\mathbb Z)$ returned only general references on Chern classes and Chern–Weil theory; no follow-up work explicitly constructing the higher classes $c_q$ for $\varepsilon$-hermitian variation structures was found. The problem appears not to have a documented resolution, but the search evidence is inconclusive.

status_evidence.title: Chern class - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Chern classes are characteristic classes associated to complex vector bundles, introduced by S.-S. Chern.
status_evidence.claim: General background on Chern classes; no mention of Wall-type variation-structure analogues.

status_evidence.title: Characterising Ball Quotients through their (higher) Chern Numbers
status_evidence.snippet: Little is known so far concerning the higher Chern classes.
status_evidence.claim: Higher Chern-type invariants remain an active and incompletely understood topic, with no specific result on variation structures.
